Maya (Design): Dropping the mobile responsive handoff here. Updated builds on staging show three behaviors: full table, compressed rows, stacked cards. Looking for quick sign-off on breakpoints, focus behavior, and copy for screen readers. :hand:
Ravi (Design): Nice! Quick thought: compressed rows should keep the primary action visible without swiping. If title wraps to two lines at 360px we may need micro-typography adjustments or reduce avatar size.
Elaine (Frontend): On the prototype the breakpoints are 540px (table -> compressed rows) and 380px (compressed -> cards). CSS snippet we used: 
```
@media (max-width: 540px) { .results-table .full-row { max-height: 56px } }
@media (max-width: 380px) { .results-table { display: none } .stacked-cards { display: block } }
```
Elaine (Frontend): Note: compressed rows still use table semantics (role=\"row\") but we apply `aria-rowindex` and hide secondary columns visually. Cards use role=\"list\" and role=\"listitem\" per Lina's earlier recommendation.
Lina (Accessibility): Confirming: keep table semantics as long as the DOM structure is a table. If we swap to a non-table DOM at small widths, ensure `role=\"list\"` + `aria-label=\"Results\"` and each card exposes a linkable heading (h3 + <a>) so screen reader users can jump. Also add `aria-live=\"polite\"` for the filter open/close announcement.
Jon (PM): Copy tweak: header should read "Filter results" (not just "Filters") and the clear all button should be labeled "Clear filters" for assistive tech. Also for the floating sort control label it should say "Sort by" with the current criteria visible.
Maya (Design): Agreed on copy. I'll update the figma frames and the spec: compressed-row spacing 12px, avatar 32px -> 28px at <=420px, title font-size 14 -> 13 at <=360px. Will add annotations for the floating sort pill (16px margin from top of results).
Elaine (Frontend): iOS keyboard note: when the filter sheet opens and an input is focused, Safari shrinks visual viewport which causes the sheet's bottom actions to be covered. Plan: use `visualViewport` listener and toggle `.keyboard-open` that applies `transform: translateY(-env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` and increase bottom padding for the action row. Will test on physical devices.
Ravi (Design): Could we also make the sheet draggable to dismiss? We used that elsewhere, feels natural on phones. But need clear affordance and not conflict with inner list scrolling.
Lina (Accessibility): If draggable, ensure the drag handle is reachable and has `aria-hidden` for screen readers and provide a visible close button with `aria-label=\"Close filters\"`. The drag-to-dismiss must not cancel keyboard dismiss events.
Elaine (Frontend): Drag-to-dismiss adds complexity but doable using `touch-action` and `pointer-events`. We'll prototype after keyboard fixes. For now prioritize stable breakpoints and ARIA.
Jon (PM): Analytics ask: we want an event when layout flips (table->compressed->cards) and when keyboard was open during filter submit. Add those instrument calls to the PR.
Maya (Design): Noted. I'll include tracking ids in the spec (filter.layout_change, filter.keyboard_open_submit).
Elaine (Frontend): One more nit: long table cells currently overflow instead of ellipsis in compressed mode. Will add `text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden;` and make title a link with `aria-describedby` pointing to meta text for screen readers.
QABot: test-plan: 1) devices: iPhone 12/13 Pro, iPhone SE (2nd gen), Pixel 6, Foldable emulator; 2) test breakpoints @ 540 & 380; 3) keyboard interactions w/ input focus; 4) screen reader flows NVDA/VoiceOver; 5) preserve selected row after navigation back; 6) sticky sort pill stays visible on scroll.
Ravi (Design): Small visual change request: in cards mode make secondary metadata lighter color (#6B7280) and truncate chips with +n indicator when overflow.
Lina (Accessibility): For chips ensure they are keyboard tabbable and exposed using `role=\"button\"` with `aria-pressed` when active. Also ensure color contrast meets 4.5:1 for text on the primary chips.
Elaine (Frontend): Will update PR to include chip roles, ellipsis rules, sticky sort pill via `position: sticky; top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 16px);` and event instrumentation. Planning to open PR today referencing ticket #INF-824.
Maya (Design): Thanks — I'll add QA checklist items to the ticket and upload the final frames. Quick ask: folks please try staging on a real device and comment inline on figma for any spacing or keyboard oddities.
Jon (PM): Adding this to next week's design sync. If no major issues from device tests, we'll ship the compressed breakpoint change in the next minor release. :shipit:
Elaine (Frontend): Link to staging build: https://staging.redwood.internal/mobile-filters-192 (build 2026.03.23-14). Drop screenshots here.
Maya (Design): Awesome, closing this thread after we get physical device checks. Thanks everyone. :tada:
